title: 9th Sitting of First session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened with questions to the Minister of Economic Development, Transport and Trade about the China free trade agreement, restaurant businesses and the dollar shortage, and nine other members asked follow-ups. An urgent motion by Dr Ahmed Shamheed on the planned dismissal of more than 13,000 state-company employees was put to a vote and did not pass (12 for, 39 against). The Speaker's desk sent the names of 14 newly appointed ministers to the committee that examines government accountability, two items had their first reading, and debate on a resolution about government spending against the 2026 budget began and was still running at the end of this part. This part picks up in the middle of the debate on a resolution from North Galolhu asking MPs to say whether they think government spending goes against the 2026 state budget the Majlis passed. The first speaker in this part (Vaikaradhoo) was finishing a speech that began in part 1; three more members then spoke, all defending the government's spending, debt repayments and economic handling. The chair ended the debate and put the resolution to a vote, where 9 members said yes and 36 said no, so it was not accepted. The next sitting was set for 9:00 on Tuesday 21 April 2026. Some of the text is garbled, so the gist of each speech is approximate.

speakers.name: Mohamed Saeed
positions: As Minister, said the FTA was negotiated with industry and agencies, and that restaurant franchises operate under set conditions.
Said Maldivian exporters can send 296 seafood items to China at zero duty under the FTA.
Said BML sold US$106.2 million in the first three months of 2026, 142 percent more than the same period of 2025.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Raised fuel for fishermen, a reported MVR 1.6 billion fall in customs duty after the FTA, and a halted port.
Moved an urgent motion on the announced cut of over 13,000 state-company staff, citing the Constitution and the Employment Act.
In debate, disputed claims of growing reserves (US$588m end-2023, US$583m end-2025), defended past sukuk financing and objected to cutting 13,000 jobs.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked why restaurants, reserved for Maldivians under foreign investment policy, were opened to Chinese firms under the China FTA, and whether industry was consulted.
Asked what difference the FTA has made to prices and what benefit the ministry has seen in the market.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Asked whether foreign direct investment permits only Chinese parties to operate here, and raised small Maldivian restaurants' position under the FTA.
Said government spending follows the budget, that earlier loans and a large sukuk repayment weigh on the budget, and that housing and hospital work is moving ahead.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Recalled a pre-election pledge to lower the dollar rate within two years and asked when the buying rate will come down.
In debate, said the budget since 2025 does not show where money is spent, citing the 2025 budget's MVR 900 million direct cash transfer line.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said the resolution is important and that prices of goods, fuel, the dollar and building materials have risen throughout the government's term.
Said PNC MPs report the President promised regular meetings with ruling-party members but has not held them.
Said no new building has started in his three islands and asked what the MVR 110 billion of spending delivered.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Said cutting import duty on Chinese fish products hurts fishermen and that guesthouses were opened to Chinese firms; asked whether any impact study was done.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked when the dollar rate will fall, where the banking boats are, and when the Development Bank last opened.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Asked whether payments on foreign loans and sukuk must be made in rufiyaa or dollars.
Asked whether any MDP government changed law or regulation to make restaurants a Maldivian-only business.
Asked which businesses are currently reserved for Maldivians only.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Said state companies have not paid small and medium firms for two to three years, pushing some toward bankruptcy; asked what the ministry has done.
Asked whether money is owed to STC.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Asked about reports that BML has halted dollar support for telegraphic transfers for businesses until month end, and what the fix is.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Said BML has not halted dollar support for telegraphic transfers, as far as he knows.
Asked whether any analysis was made of the FTA's positive effect on goods and on small and medium businesses.

speakers.name: Ahmed Thariq
positions: Said the US$524 million sukuk due on 8 April 2026 was repaid from state reserves.
Said the 2021 sukuk (US$500m, with US$250m extra) was issued under the MDP, and that about US$700m in interest has been paid.
Credited the repayment to government decisions, support from India and China, and no new foreign borrowing.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Rejected the resolution's premise, saying the government spends within the budget, and regretted its being brought as urgent business.
Said the government settled dues to fishermen and businesses and freed mortgaged schools and Dharumavantha Hospital.
Criticised the previous government's printing of about MVR 8 billion.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Described the resolution as aimed at the previous MDP government's record and called claims about state finances false.
Said the Sovereign Development Fund's usable balance is US$2 million.
Said Aasandha owed MVR 1.6 billion to overseas hospitals and MVR 400 million locally, and criticised MVR 8 billion of money printing.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said projects proceed across islands under the budget and not every island can move at the same pace, citing Velidhoo's reclamation and air-taxi link.
Said the government capped prices of 26 staple items through STO from October 2025, lowering prices such as oranges and apples.
Said the state sets staffing after studying conditions, and noted the opposition earlier complained there were too many state-company staff.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Argued the budget lists planned spending clearly, so the resolution has no basis; said large debt repayments and global conditions limit what the government can spend.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Called the resolution baseless; said earlier governments used supplementary budgets and left unpaid contractors, and urged the opposition to avoid steps that could hurt tourism.

decisions: Urgent motion by Dr Ahmed Shamheed on state-company job cuts was not accepted for debate (12 for, 39 against, 0 abstain; 26 needed).
The names of 12 ministers appointed on 14 April 2026 were referred to the committee that examines government accountability.
The names of 2 ministers appointed on 15 April 2026 were referred to the same committee.
The Fisheries Act (Law 2019/14) amendment bill was read for the first time.
The resolution on Public Service Media was read for the first time.
Debate on the North Galolhu resolution on government spending against the 2026 budget continued with no vote in this part.
The North Galolhu resolution seeking MPs' views on government spending against the 2026 budget was not accepted at the vote.
The chair ended the debate on the resolution and moved to the vote.
Next sitting set for 9:00 on Tuesday 21 April 2026.

votes.what: Urgent motion (Rule 192) by Dr Ahmed Shamheed on the government's decision to cut over 13,000 state-company employees: whether to debate it (93 members, 52 present, 51 voted)
Accept the North Galolhu resolution on government spending against the 2026 state budget
